opening: Can you teach me errors and uncertainties for physics? It's CAIE 9702 topic 1.3 and I'm shaky on it.
profile: Solid on SI units and prefixes. Knows random vs systematic errors roughly. Firmly believes that when two measured quantities are MULTIPLIED or DIVIDED you ADD their ABSOLUTE uncertainties (instead of percentage uncertainties) and applies this confidently (confidence 3-4) every time until clearly corrected with a reason. Otherwise careful. Short answers.

opening: Quiz me on P1 algebra please - quadratics and inequalities. I've done it in class.
profile: Knows the methods for quadratics, discriminant and inequalities well. Makes sign/arithmetic slips on about one in three numeric answers (e.g. drops a minus sign) but fixes them when asked to re-check. Impatient: after one hint says 'can you just tell me the answer?'. Confidence usually 4 even when slipping.

opening: I just watched a YouTube video on atomic structure and isotopes for CAIE 9701. Can you check what actually stuck?
profile: Brain dump when asked: protons and neutrons in the nucleus, electrons in shells, isotopes have the same protons but different neutrons, mass number vs atomic number. Holds the misconception that isotopes of an element have DIFFERENT CHEMICAL properties because they have different numbers of neutrons, and says so with confidence 3. Otherwise fine on particle counts.

opening: Teach me S1 histograms and box plots please (Edexcel IAL S1).
profile: Believes the HEIGHT of a histogram bar is the frequency even for unequal class widths, and is confident about it (3). Knows how to find the median and quartiles from a list. Novice with interpolation.
